mainTopic: Stories of צדיקים and of fasts for rain: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת, אלעזר איש בירתא, and leaders whose prayers were answered
overview: This amud tells a series of stories about צדיקים and about fasts for rain. It begins with רבי יוסי בר אבין, who left his teacher רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת because the teacher was so strict that he spared neither his own son nor his own daughter. The גמרא tells both stories, and then the story of רבי יוסי's donkey, which would carry home only the exact rent. Next comes אלעזר איש בירתא, who gave his daughter's dowry money to orphans. His storehouse was miraculously filled with wheat, and he refused to benefit from it. The גמרא then returns to fasts for rain. רבי יהודה נשיאה and later רב נחמן were humbled, and rain came. רבי יוחנן rules that a public fast does not need to be accepted the day before, and אושעיא rebukes the house of the נשיא with the parable of the bride's eyes. Two prayer leaders bring rain through their quiet good deeds. The amud ends as רבה begins to explain why his fasts fail where רב יהודה's succeeded, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's rule about taking a fish out of the water on שבת
steps.stepSummary: While רב אשי is reviewing his learning, he recites a הלכה from שמואל: if someone takes a fish out of the water on שבת, he is liable once a סלע-sized area of the fish has dried.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he heard him reviewing his learning. שמואל said: If someone takes a fish out of the sea on שבת, once an area the size of a סלע coin has dried on it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The story begins with רבי יוסי בר אבין overhearing רב אשי reviewing a הלכה of שמואל. This sets up the conversation between the two that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fish that has dried out this much can no longer survive. So taking it out of the water counts as killing it, which is the מלאכה of שוחט on שבת. The size of a סלע is the point at which the fish is considered as good as dead.

keyTerms.meaning: Reviews or recites his learning out loud
One who pulls something out (of the water)
A coin; used here as a measure of size

phrases.english: One day he heard him reviewing his learning:
Shmuel said:
One who removes a fish from the sea on Shabbat,
once an area the size of a sela has dried on it, he is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable for killing a living creature on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד שַׁמְעֵיהּ דְּקָא גָרֵיס, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing a fish from the water on שבת makes one liable once a סלע-sized area of it has dried.

steps.title: Adding the detail 'between its fins'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין says that the rule should include a detail: the dried area must be between the fins.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let the Master also say: 'and between its fins!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין suggests that רב אשי's version of שמואל's rule is missing a detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not rejecting שמואל's rule. He is sharpening it: the dried spot that counts must be in the area between the fins. That detail is what makes the fish unable to survive.

keyTerms.meaning: And let the Master say (a suggested change or addition)

phrases.english: He said to him: And let the Master say
'and between its fins'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלֵימָא מָר וּבֵין סְנַפִּירָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the case in שמואל's rule from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of שמואל's rule as רב אשי recited it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule as recited leaves out where on the fish the dried area must be.

steps.title: רב אשי asks whose addition this is
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks: isn't this addition the teaching of רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין? Why not say it in his name?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold that רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין said that?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי recognizes the addition. He asks why the speaker is quoting it as if it needs no name, when it belongs to a specific sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי knows that the detail 'between its fins' was taught by רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין. He doesn't realize that this sage is the very person standing in front of him. This sets up the surprise answer in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: And doesn't the Master hold

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהִיא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי אָבִין אַמְרַהּ?
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Avin said that one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר דְּהָהִיא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן רַבִּי אָבִין אַמְרַהּ
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the addition was not said in the name of רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין.

steps.title: 'I am he'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין reveals that he himself is the author of the teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am he.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker answers simply that he is רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why he did not quote it in anyone's name: it is his own teaching. It also tells us that he is now learning in רב אשי's study hall, which sets up the next question.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am he.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The speaker is himself רבי יוסי בן רבי אבין.

steps.title: Didn't you used to learn with רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether he used to learn regularly before רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת, and he says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't the Master used to be found regularly before רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי confirms a fact about רבי יוסי בר אבין's past. This sets up his real question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that רב אשי knows who he is speaking with, he recalls that this sage was a student of רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת. The answer 'yes' leads straight into the question of why he left.

keyTerms.meaning: Yokrat, the hometown of רבי יוסי

phrases.english: He said to him: And wasn't it before
Rabbi Yosei of Yokrat
that the Master was regularly found?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמִן יוֹקֶרֶת הֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ מָר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether he used to be a student of רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת.

steps.title: Why did you leave him and come here?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks why he left רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת and came to learn here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And what is the reason the Master left him and came here?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the real question that the previous step was leading up to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving one's רבי was unusual, so רב אשי wants to know the reason. The answer opens the main story of this section.

phrases.english: He said to him: And what is the reason
that the Master left him and came here?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי טַעְמָא שַׁבְקֵיהּ מָר וַאֲתָא הָכָא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason he left his teacher.

steps.title: A man with no mercy on his own children
steps.stepSummary: He explains that he left because רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת had no mercy even on his own son and daughter, so he could not expect mercy for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A man who had no mercy on his son and no mercy on his daughter, how would he have mercy on me?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין explains that his teacher's extreme strictness frightened him away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues by logic: if his teacher was harsh even with his own children, a mere student could surely expect no gentler treatment. The גמרא will now tell the stories behind this claim, starting with the son.

phrases.english: He said to him: A man who on his son
and on his daughter did not have mercy,
how would he have mercy on me?!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא דְּעַל בְּרֵיהּ וְעַל בְּרַתֵּיה לָא חָס
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He left because his teacher was so strict that he spared neither his son nor his daughter.

steps.title: What happened with his son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the story of the son was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story of his son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for the details of the son's story. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim in step 7 needs support, so the גמרא opens a new story to explain what happened to the son.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What is the story?)

phrases.english: His son — what is it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The details of the incident with the son.

steps.title: The son makes a fig tree give fruit for the hungry workers
steps.stepSummary: The father's hired workers were hungry because food was late. The son told a fig tree to give its fruit, and it did, and the workers ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he hired workers in the field. It got late and he did not bring them bread. They said to his son: We are hungry! They were sitting under a fig tree. He said: Fig tree, fig tree! Bring out your fruit, so my father's workers can eat. It brought out fruit and they ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by telling the miracle story of the son and the fig tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son acted out of real kindness: the workers were starving, and their food was late. The tree gave fruit even though it was not the season for it, which shows the son's power in prayer. That detail of the fruit coming out of season becomes the key to the father's reaction.

phrases.english: One day he had hired for himself
workers in the field,

phrases.aramaic: נְגַהּ לְהוּ וְלָא אַיְיתִי לְהוּ רִיפְתָּא,
phrases.english: it grew late for them and he did not bring them food,
they said to his son: We are starving!
They were sitting under a fig tree,
he said: Fig tree, fig tree!
Bring out your fruit, so my father's workers may eat.
It brought out fruit, and they ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד הֲווֹ אֲגִרִי לֵיהּ אֲגִירֵי בְּדַבְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son made a fig tree give fruit out of season to feed the workers.

steps.title: The father arrives and apologizes for being late
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת arrives and tells the workers not to be upset, because he was delayed doing a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile his father came. He said to them: Don't hold it against me. The reason I was late is that I was busy with a מצוה, and I have been traveling until just now.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the father arrives and explains why the food was late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father does not yet know about the miracle. He apologizes to his workers and explains that a מצוה kept him busy. This sets up the workers' reply.

phrases.english: In the meantime his father came
he said to them: Do not hold it against me,
for the reason I was late is that I was busy with a מצוה,
and until just now I was traveling.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father explains that his lateness came from being busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: The workers bless him and tell what happened
steps.stepSummary: The workers bless the father to be satisfied the way his son satisfied them. When he asks how, they tell him the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: May the Merciful One satisfy you the way your son satisfied us. He said: From where? They said: This and this is what happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The workers reveal that the son already fed them. The father asks how, and they tell him about the miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The workers mean their words as a blessing, but the news makes the father learn about the miracle. This leads straight to his sharp reaction.

phrases.english: They said to him: May the Merciful One satisfy you
just as your son satisfied us.
He said to them: From where?
They said: Such and such an incident happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: רַחֲמָנָא לַישְׂבְּעָךְ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאַשְׂבְּעַן בְּרָךְ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father learns that his son made the fig tree give fruit.

steps.title: The father's words: you will be taken before your time
steps.stepSummary: The father tells his son: since you troubled your Creator to make a fig tree give fruit before its time, you will be taken from the world before your time. And so it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My son, you troubled your Creator to make the fig tree give its fruit before its time. You will be gathered in (die) before your time.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the father's harsh words to his son. This proves רבי יוסי בר אבין's claim that his teacher had no mercy even on his own son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father did not object to feeding the workers. He objected to troubling ה׳ to change nature for something that could have been handled normally. The punishment matches the act: fruit before its time, so death before its time.

keyTerms.meaning: Will be gathered in, meaning will die

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי בר אבין left רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת because of his extreme strictness. The son's miracle made a tree give fruit before its time, and the father said the son would die before his time. This is the measure-for-measure idea: the punishment matches the act.
steps.confusionAlert: The son is not punished for feeding the workers, which was a kind act. He is held responsible for troubling ה׳ to break the order of nature without real need.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story shows how carefully great צדיקים treated their power in prayer, and why רבי יוסי בר אבין felt his teacher's strictness was too much to bear.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, אַתָּה הִטְרַחְתָּ אֶת קוֹנְךָ
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, you troubled your Creator
to make a fig tree bring out its fruit not in its time —
you will be gathered in not in your time.
phrases.notes: And indeed, the son died young.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the son's story and proves the claim made in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because the son troubled ה׳ to make the tree give fruit before its time, he died before his time. This proves how strict רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת was, even with his own son.

steps.title: What was the story of his daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the story about רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story of his daughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the second family story about רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת. This line sets up the next story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said he punished both his son and his daughter. It just finished the son's story, so now it turns to the daughter's story.

phrases.english: His daughter, what is it (what was her story)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the finished son story to the daughter story, which follows the same pattern.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened with רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת's daughter.

steps.title: A man peeks at the beautiful daughter through the fence
steps.stepSummary: His daughter was very beautiful. One day he saw a man making a hole in the fence to look at her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a beautiful daughter. One day he saw a certain man digging a hole in the fence and looking at her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question: the daughter was so beautiful that a man broke through a fence just to look at her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the problem. Her beauty was causing people to act wrongly. The man was not only glancing at her. He was making a hole in order to stare.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman of beauty, very beautiful
A fence or hedge made of branches

phrases.english: He had a daughter who was very beautiful.
One day he saw a certain man
who was making a hole in the fence
and was looking at her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 13 by starting the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The daughter's beauty led a man to break through a fence to look at her.

steps.title: The man explains why he is looking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי asks the man what he is doing. The man answers that if he cannot marry her, he should at least get to look at her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is this? He said to him: My teacher, if I did not merit to marry her, shall I not at least merit to see her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת confronts the man. The man defends himself by saying that looking is the least he deserves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man's answer shows that he does not see anything wrong in what he is doing. This is what makes רבי יוסי realize that his daughter's beauty is a real cause of sin for others.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is this?
He said to him: My teacher,
if I did not merit to marry her,
shall I not merit at least to see her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with a short conversation between רבי יוסי and the man.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man openly justifies looking at her, which shows how much she is causing others to stumble.

steps.title: Return to your dust
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי tells his daughter that she is causing people distress, and that she should return to her dust so people will not sin because of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: My daughter, you are causing people distress. Return to your dust, and let people not stumble because of you.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the ending of the daughter's story. רבי יוסי speaks words that cause his daughter to die, so that she will not lead others to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the son's story. Both children were taken from the world through their father's words. Here the reason is that she was leading people to stumble.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת was extremely strict. He was ready to have his own children taken from the world rather than allow a misuse of a miracle (the son) or allow people to sin (the daughter).

phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter,
you are causing people distress.
Return to your dust,
and let people not stumble because of you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ending of the daughter story, in reaction to the man's words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The daughter was taken from the world so that she would not cause people to sin.

steps.title: The donkey that took only exact payment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי had a donkey that people rented. At night they sent it home with the rent on its back. If the money was too much or too little, it would not go.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had a certain donkey. When people rented it each day, in the evening they would send it back with its rent on its back, and it would go to its owner's house. If they added to the payment or took some away, it would not go.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new miracle story about רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת. His donkey would only go home with exactly the right payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle shows how careful רבי יוסי was about honesty. Even his animal would not carry money that was not exactly his.

phrases.english: He had a certain donkey.
When people rented it each day,
in the evening they would send it back
with its rent on its back,
and it would come to its owner's house.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי טָפוּ לַהּ אוֹ בָּצְרִי לַהּ —
phrases.english: But if they added to it or took away from it,
it would not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, separate miracle story about the same person, רבי יוסי דמן יוקרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's donkey miraculously refused to carry anything other than the exact payment.

steps.title: The forgotten sandals
steps.stepSummary: One day someone forgot a pair of sandals on the donkey. It would not move until they took them off.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day they forgot a pair of sandals on it, and it did not go until they took them off. Then it went.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an example of the donkey's miracle. Even a forgotten item that was not part of the payment stopped it from leaving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the donkey refused anything extra, even by accident, and not only extra money. The sandals did not belong to its owner, so it would not take them.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָא חַד אִינְּשׁוֹ זוּגָא דְסַנְדָּלֵי עֲלַהּ,
phrases.english: One day they forgot a pair of sandals on it,
and it did not go
until they took them off it,
and then it went.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹמָא חַד אִינְּשׁוֹ זוּגָא דְסַנְדָּלֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a specific incident that shows the donkey's miracle in action.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The donkey would not leave even with forgotten sandals on it, because they were not its owner's.

steps.title: The charity collectors hide from אלעזר איש בירתא
steps.stepSummary: The גבאי צדקה used to hide from אלעזר איש בירתא, because he would give them everything he had with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר איש בירתא: when the גבאי צדקה saw him, they would hide from him, because he would give them everything he had with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about a different צדיק, אלעזר איש בירתא, who was extremely generous with צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually people hide from collectors. Here the collectors hid from the giver, because they did not want him to give away everything he owned.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not get it backwards: the collectors are the ones hiding, not אלעזר. They were protecting him from his own generosity.

phrases.english: Elazar of Birta:

phrases.aramaic: כַּד הֲווֹ חָזוּ לֵיהּ גַּבָּאֵי צְדָקָה
phrases.english: when the charity collectors would see him,
they would hide from him,
because whatever he had with him
he would give to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about a new person, still on the theme of the miracles of צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלעזר איש בירתא gave away everything he had to צדקה, so the collectors avoided him.

steps.title: On the way to buy his daughter's dowry
steps.stepSummary: One day אלעזר went to the market to buy a dowry for his daughter. The collectors saw him and hid.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he was going up to the market to buy a dowry for his daughter. The charity collectors saw him and hid from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the scene for the main story. אלעזר has money for his own daughter's wedding, and the collectors try to avoid him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This raises the stakes. This time the money was for his own daughter's נדוניא, a very important family need, so the collectors had even more reason to hide.

phrases.english: One day he was going up to the market
to buy a dowry for his daughter.
The charity collectors saw him
and hid from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general description of אלעזר to a specific day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with dowry money for his own daughter, the collectors hid from him.

steps.title: He chases them and asks what they are collecting for
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר ran after the collectors and made them swear to tell him what מצוה they were collecting for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and ran after them. He said to them: I make you swear: what are you busy with?
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of being glad they hid, אלעזר chases the collectors and demands to know what cause they are collecting for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how eager he was to give. He did not wait to be asked. He went after the chance to do the מצוה.

phrases.english: He went and ran after them.
He said to them: I make you swear,
what are you busy with?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל וּרְהַט בָּתְרַיְיהוּ, אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַשְׁבַּעְתִּיכוּ בְּמַאי עָסְקִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אלעזר reacts to the collectors hiding by chasing them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which צדקה cause the collectors were raising money for.

steps.title: For an orphan boy and an orphan girl
steps.stepSummary: The collectors answer that they are raising money for an orphan boy and an orphan girl to get married.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: For an orphan boy and an orphan girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The collectors answer that they are collecting for the wedding of two orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a direct comparison. אלעזר was on his way to pay for his own daughter's wedding, and they were collecting for orphans' wedding. The question now is whose wedding comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan boy and an orphan girl

phrases.english: They said to him: With an orphan boy and an orphan girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אלעזר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were collecting to marry off an orphan boy and an orphan girl.

steps.title: The orphans come before my daughter
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר swore that the orphans come before his own daughter, and gave them everything he had with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I swear by the Temple service that they come before my daughter. He took everything he had with him and gave it to them.
steps.whatsHappening: אלעזר decides that the orphans' needs come first, and he gives them all the money he brought for his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not state his reason, but presumably it is that orphans have no one else to provide for them, while his daughter has a father. He backs this up with a strong oath and then acts on it at once.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Temple service (a form of oath)

steps.whyThisMatters: It is a powerful picture of putting someone else's need ahead of your own family's, which is why it leads to the miracle that comes next.

phrases.english: He said to them: (I swear) by the Temple service
that they come before my daughter.
He took everything that he had with him
and gave it to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הָעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁהֵן קוֹדְמִין לְבִתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אלעזר responds to the collectors' answer with his decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The orphans' wedding came before his own daughter's, so he gave them everything.

steps.title: One coin left, spent on wheat
steps.stepSummary: He had one זוז left. He bought wheat with it, brought it home, and threw it into his storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was left with one זוז. He bought wheat for himself with it, went up, and threw it into the granary.
steps.whatsHappening: אלעזר is left with almost nothing. He buys a little wheat and puts it in his storehouse. This sets up the miracle that comes in the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail of one coin and a small amount of wheat in the granary prepares for what follows. The story is not finished yet, and it continues next.

phrases.english: He was left with one zuz.
He bought himself wheat,
and went up and threw it into the granary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what was left after he gave everything away, and sets up the coming miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After his giving, he was left with only one coin's worth of wheat in his granary.

steps.title: The wife asks what her husband brought home
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר's wife comes home and asks their daughter what her father brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife came and said to her daughter: What did your father bring?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. אלעזר's wife wants to know what he brought home from the market, since he had gone out to buy a dowry. This question sets up the discovery that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife expects a dowry or food. The reader already knows he gave everything away and threw only one זוז's worth of wheat into the storehouse. The question builds tension before the miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife (literally, 'the one of his house')

phrases.english: His wife came
she said to her daughter:
What did your father bring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after אלעזר threw the wheat into his storehouse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did אלעזר bring home from the market?

steps.title: The daughter says it was thrown into the storehouse
steps.stepSummary: The daughter answers that whatever he brought, he threw into the storehouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to her: Whatever he brought, he threw into the storehouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter answers her mother. Whatever her father brought is in the storehouse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer points the mother to the storehouse. That is where the miracle is waiting. The daughter does not seem to know what is inside.

phrases.english: She said to her: Whatever he brought,
he threw it into the storehouse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mother's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whatever he brought is in the storehouse.

steps.title: The storehouse is miraculously full of wheat
steps.stepSummary: The mother opens the storehouse and finds it overflowing with wheat, so full that the door will not open.
steps.simpleTranslation: She went to open the door of the storehouse. She saw the storehouse full of wheat, spilling out through the door's hinge-hole, and the door could not open because of the wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the miracle. A single זוז of wheat has become a storehouse so full that wheat pours out of the door and the door is stuck shut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלעזר gave everything to the orphans and kept almost nothing. Heaven repaid him with a full storehouse. The detail that the door could not open shows how huge the miracle was.

keyTerms.meaning: The hinge-hole or socket of the door

phrases.english: She came to open the door of the storehouse,
she saw the storehouse was full of wheat
and it was coming out through the door's hinge-hole,
phrases.notes: Sefaria translates this as 'doorknob'. The point is the same: wheat was squeezing out of every opening.

phrases.english: and the door would not open because of the wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mother goes to the storehouse the daughter mentioned and discovers the miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלעזר's generosity was rewarded with a miraculously full storehouse.

steps.title: The daughter tells her father about the miracle
steps.stepSummary: The daughter runs to the בית מדרש and tells אלעזר to come see what ה׳ did for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: His daughter went to the study hall and said to him: Come and see what the One Who loves you has done for you!
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter brings the news to her father in the בית מדרש. This sets up his surprising reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The One Who loves you' refers to ה׳. The daughter sees the miracle as a gift from ה׳ to her father. She expects him to be happy and to enjoy it.

keyTerms.meaning: The One Who loves you, meaning ה׳

phrases.english: His daughter went to the study hall,
she said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה מָה עָשָׂה לְךָ אוֹהַבְךָ!
phrases.english: Come and see what the One Who loves you did for you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The family reports the miracle to אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter credits ה׳ with the miracle and calls her father to see it.

steps.title: אלעזר declares the wheat holy and refuses to benefit
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר swears that the wheat is הקדש for his daughter. She may take from it only like any poor Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: I swear by the Temple service, this wheat is consecrated as far as you are concerned. You have a share in it only like one of the poor people of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of celebrating, אלעזר makes the wheat הקדש so that his family will not personally benefit from a miracle. This ends the story of אלעזר איש בירתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not want to use up his merits by enjoying a miracle, and he did not want to benefit from one. His daughter may still take from it, but only as a poor person collecting צדקה, not as the owner's daughter. The man who gave everything to orphans stays the same until the very end.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Temple service, a form of oath
Consecrated property that may not be used for personal benefit

steps.whatToRemember: אלעזר איש בירתא gave all his money to orphans. Even when he was rewarded with a miracle, he refused to benefit from it and turned it into charity for the poor.

phrases.english: He said to her: By the Temple service,
they are consecrated property for you,
and you have no share in them
except as one of the poor of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: הָעֲבוֹדָה, הֲרֵי הֵן הֶקְדֵּשׁ עָלַיִךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אלעזר responds to his daughter's news by refusing personal benefit.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A truly righteous person does not want to benefit from a miracle. He gives even miraculous gifts to the poor.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה declares a fast, but no rain comes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to fasting for rain. רבי יהודה נשיאה declared a fast and prayed, but it did not rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה declared a fast. He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins about fasting for rain. This step sets up the problem: the fast and prayers did not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts back to the main theme of the מסכת, which is public fasts for rain. As נשיא, the leader of the Jewish people, רבי יהודה נשיאה had the authority to declare a public fast. The prayer failed, and that sets up his reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia decreed a fast,
he prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, returning to the topic of fasting for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast was declared by the נשיא, and the prayers were not answered.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה laments his own low level
steps.stepSummary: He compares himself to שמואל הרמתי, whose prayers brought rain, and cries out in grief over his generation and his own leadership.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: How great is the difference between שמואל הרמתי and יהודה בן גמליאל! Woe to the generation that is stuck with this! Woe to the one in whose days this happened!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה blames himself for the lack of rain. He says he is nothing like שמואל הנביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל הרמתי prayed, and rain fell even in summer. רבי יהודה נשיאה sees the failure of his prayer as proof that his own spiritual level is low. He calls himself by his plain name, 'יהודה בן גמליאל', without any title, which shows his humility.

keyTerms.meaning: שמואל הנביא from the town of Rama
Stuck, or caught in a bad situation

phrases.english: He said: How great is the difference
between Samuel of Rama and Yehuda ben Gamliel!
Woe to the generation that is stuck like this,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לוֹ לְמִי שֶׁעָלְתָה בְּיָמָיו כָּךְ!
phrases.english: woe to the one in whose days this happened!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: כַּמָּה אִיכָּא מִשְּׁמוּאֵל הָרָמָתִי לִיהוּדָה בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: His reaction to the failed fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leader takes personal responsibility for the failure of the prayer.

steps.title: His humility brings the rain
steps.stepSummary: He became upset and broken-hearted, and then rain came.
steps.simpleTranslation: He became upset, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: His broken heart worked where the fast alone had not. The rain came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain did not come in answer to the formal fast. It came after the leader truly humbled himself. The lesson is that sincere humility and a broken heart can bring the answer to a prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: He became upset, humbled, or broken-hearted

steps.whatToRemember: A humble, broken heart can accomplish what a formal fast alone did not.

phrases.english: He became upset, and rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The outcome of his self-humbling.

steps.title: A fast is declared without telling רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש in time
steps.stepSummary: The house of the נשיא declared a fast. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש were not told until the morning of the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of the נשיא decreed a fast, and they did not inform רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. In the morning they informed them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. Two great sages learn about a public fast only on the morning of the fast itself. This sets up a halachic question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must accept a fast during מנחה on the day before. Since they only found out in the morning, they never had the chance to accept it. That creates the problem discussed next.

phrases.english: The house of the Nasi decreed a fast,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אוֹדְעִינְהוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: and they did not inform Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish.
In the morning they informed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא, וְלָא אוֹדְעִינְהוּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about a fast declared by the נשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sages learned about the public fast only on the morning of the fast.

steps.title: ריש לקיש worries they did not accept the fast the night before
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש points out to רבי יוחנן that they never accepted the fast the evening before.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: But we did not accept the fast upon ourselves from the evening before!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש raises a halachic concern. Does the fast count for them if they did not accept it the day before?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual fast must be accepted during מנחה of the previous day. ריש לקיש asks whether that rule also applies to a public fast declared by the נשיא. The question is phrased as a statement, but it works as a request for a ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: 'From the evening' does not mean the night of the fast. It refers to the day before, when a fast is normally accepted during מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
But we did not accept it upon ourselves from the evening before!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the halachic problem created by the late notice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a public fast need to be accepted by each individual on the day before?

steps.title: We follow the community
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that individuals are drawn after the community, so no personal acceptance is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are drawn after them, meaning the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rules that a public fast counts even without personal acceptance. Individuals are simply part of the community's fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personal acceptance is needed only for a private fast. A public fast is binding because of the community's decree, and each person is automatically included. This settles ריש לקיש's concern.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical halacha: a תענית ציבור does not need to be personally accepted the day before.
steps.whatToRemember: A private fast must be accepted the day before. A public fast does not, because each person follows the community.

phrases.english: He said to him: We are drawn after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's concern.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Individuals follow the community, so a public fast needs no personal acceptance the day before.

steps.title: Another fast by the house of the נשיא, but no rain
steps.stepSummary: Another time, the house of the נשיא declared a fast, and rain did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of the נשיא decreed a fast, and rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: A new short story begins with a failed fast. This sets up a teaching that hints at why it failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup is the same as in the earlier story of רבי יהודה נשיאה. This time, the explanation will come from a young scholar, not from the leader himself.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא וְלָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא.
phrases.english: The house of the Nasi decreed a fast, and rain did not come.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא וְלָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with the same opening as the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast by the house of the נשיא went unanswered.

steps.title: אושעיא זעירא quotes a verse about the eyes of the congregation
steps.stepSummary: The youngest of the sages, אושעיא זעירא, quotes a verse about an error committed by 'the eyes of the congregation'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אושעיא, the youngest of the group, taught them: 'And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation it was done in error.'
steps.whatsHappening: A young scholar begins to explain why the rain did not come. He quotes a פסוק, and the meaning will be developed in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the leaders 'the eyes of the congregation'. The hint is that the leaders, meaning the house of the נשיא, are responsible. When the leaders fall short, the whole community suffers. It is a bold message from the youngest member of the group.

keyTerms.meaning: אושעיא, the youngest member of the group of sages
The eyes of the congregation, meaning its leaders

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the full point yet. The verse is quoted as a hint, and אושעיא himself spells out what it means in the next step, with the parable of the bride.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא לְהוּ אוֹשַׁעְיָא זְעֵירָא דְּמִן חַבְרַיָּיא:
phrases.english: Oshaya, the youngest of the group, taught them:
'And it shall be, if from the eyes of the congregation'
'it was done in error.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא לְהוּ אוֹשַׁעְיָא זְעֵירָא דְּמִן חַבְרַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to explain the failed fast by hinting that the leaders are at fault.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק calls the leaders 'the eyes of the congregation', which hints that the leaders bear responsibility for the community's suffering.

steps.title: The parable of the bride's eyes
steps.stepSummary: אושעיא זעירא finishes his rebuke with a parable. If a bride's eyes are beautiful, the rest of her body needs no checking. If her eyes are flawed, her whole body must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a bride who is still in her father's house. As long as her eyes are beautiful, her whole body does not need to be checked. If her eyes are bleary, her whole body needs to be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: אושעיא זעירא continues the verse he quoted about the 'eyes of the congregation' by giving a parable about a bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'eyes' stand for the leaders, meaning the house of the נשיא. If the leaders are good, you can assume the people are good too. Since the leaders are flawed, the whole generation is now suspect, and that is why the rain did not come.

phrases.english: A parable: a bride who is in her father's house.
phrases.notes: The groom has not yet seen her.

phrases.english: As long as her eyes are beautiful —
her whole body does not need examination.
If her eyes are bleary —
her whole body needs examination.
phrases.notes: Hint: the leaders' flaws expose the whole generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the verse-based rebuke begun by אושעיא זעירא in step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flawed leaders show that the whole community needs to be examined. This explains why the נשיא's fast was not answered.

steps.title: The נשיא's servants punish אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: The servants of the נשיא come and torment אושעיא זעירא for insulting the house of the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: His servants came, put a scarf around his neck, and were tormenting him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the נשיא's servants react angrily to אושעיא זעירא's public rebuke and start hurting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rebuke was taken as an insult to the leadership, so the servants punish him physically. This sets up the townspeople's defense in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His servants (here, the servants of the נשיא)
They were tormenting or causing pain

phrases.english: His servants came
phrases.notes: Meaning the servants of the נשיא.

phrases.english: and threw a scarf around his neck,
and were tormenting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ עַבְדֵּיהּ וּרְמוֹ לֵיהּ סוּדָרָא בְּצַוְּארֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the house of the נשיא reacted to the rebuke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נשיא's servants punished אושעיא זעירא for his rebuke.

steps.title: The townspeople defend אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: The people of his town tell the servants to leave him alone. He rebukes them harshly too, but they put up with it because all his actions are for the sake of Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of his town said to them: Leave him alone, because he causes us pain too. But since we see that everything he does is for the sake of Heaven, we say nothing to him and let him be. You should also let him be.
steps.whatsHappening: The townspeople step in and defend אושעיא זעירא against the servants. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They admit that his rebukes sting, since they get rebuked as well. But his sincere motive, לשם שמים, makes his criticism worth tolerating. That reasoning is their argument for letting him go.
steps.whatToRemember: Sharp rebuke that is truly לשם שמים should be tolerated, even when it hurts.

phrases.english: The people of his town said to them:
Leave him, for he also pains us.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזֵינַן דְּכׇל מִילֵּיהּ לְשׁוּם שָׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: Since we see that all his matters are for the sake of Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ מִידֵּי וְשָׁבְקִינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: we say nothing to him and leave him be;
you too, leave him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the servants' punishment and ends the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because his intent is for Heaven's sake, his harsh rebukes are tolerated, and he should be left alone.

steps.title: אילפא's prayer brings rain after רבי's fast
steps.stepSummary: רבי declares a fast, but no rain comes. אילפא (or רבי אילפי) leads the prayers. Wind blows at 'משיב הרוח', and rain falls at 'מוריד הגשם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי declared a fast and rain did not come. אילפא (some say רבי אילפי) went down to lead the prayer before him. He said 'Who makes the wind blow', and the wind blew. He said 'Who makes the rain fall', and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story: a fast decreed by the great רבי fails, but the prayer of אילפא, who leads the service, is answered at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The immediate answer to אילפא's prayer, after רבי's fast had not brought rain, suggests that he has some special merit. This sets up רבי's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before him (to lead the prayer as חזן)
'Who makes the wind blow' (a phrase in the עמידה)

phrases.english: Rabbi decreed a fast
and rain did not come.
Ilfa went down before him
phrases.notes: The prayer leader stood in a lower spot.

phrases.english: (and some say it was Rabbi Ilfi),
he said 'Who makes the wind blow,' and the wind blew,
'Who makes the rain fall,' and the rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא וְלָא אֲתָא מִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about fasts for rain that are answered through one person's merit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אילפא's prayer as prayer leader brought rain where רבי's fast had not.

steps.title: רבי asks about אילפא's deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks the prayer leader what good deeds earned him such a fast answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are your deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks a direct question to find out what merit made this man's prayer so powerful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the question is that an answer this quick must come from a special merit. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are your deeds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the prayer in step 41 was answered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which good deed gave this prayer leader such great merit.

steps.title: אילפא provides wine for קידוש and הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: He lives in a poor town with no wine for קידוש and הבדלה. He makes the effort to bring wine so that everyone can fulfill their obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I live in a poor town that has no wine for קידוש and הבדלה. I take the trouble to bring wine for קידוש and הבדלה, and I help them fulfill their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The prayer leader answers רבי. His merit is making sure a poor town can do the מצוות of קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His deed is not about his own מצוות. He works hard so that others can keep theirs. Helping the whole community is what gave his prayer its power.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I live in a poor town
in which there is no wine for Kiddush and Havdalah.
I take the trouble and bring
phrases.notes: The text is corrected from 'and I come' to 'and I bring'.

phrases.english: wine for Kiddush and Havdalah,
and I enable them to fulfill their obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His merit is bringing wine to a poor town so that its people can fulfill קידוש and הבדלה.

steps.title: A prayer leader brings rain after רב's fast
steps.stepSummary: רב comes to a certain place and declares a fast, but no rain comes. The local שליח ציבור prays, and wind and rain come right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב came to a certain place and declared a fast, but rain did not come. The prayer leader went down before him. He said 'Who makes the wind blow', and the wind blew. He said 'Who makes the rain fall', and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story that follows the same pattern as the first, this time with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the pattern makes the lesson stronger: a hidden merit of a simple person can bring rain when a great sage's fast does not. Again, this sets up the question 'What are your deeds?'

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader, the שליח ציבור

phrases.english: Rav happened to come to a certain place,
he decreed a fast and rain did not come.
The prayer leader went down before him,
he said 'Who makes the wind blow,' and the wind blew,
he said 'Who makes the rain fall,' and the rain came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story with the same pattern as step 41.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A local prayer leader's prayer brought rain where רב's fast had not.

steps.title: רב asks about the prayer leader's deeds
steps.stepSummary: רב asks the prayer leader the same question: what are your deeds?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are your deeds?
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks what special merit this prayer leader has, just as רבי asked in the first story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as the question in step 42. The story is built to be read side by side with the first one.

phrases.english: He said to him: What are your deeds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the prayer in step 44 was answered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which good deed earned this prayer leader's prayer such a quick answer.

steps.title: The devoted teacher of children
steps.stepSummary: He is a teacher of young children. He teaches poor and rich children equally and takes nothing from those who cannot pay. He uses fish from his pond to coax and calm students who slack off, until they come back and learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am a teacher of young children. I teach the children of the poor the same as the children of the rich. Whoever cannot pay, I take nothing from him. I have a fishpond, and any child who neglects his studies, I win him over with the fish. We settle him and soothe him until he comes and reads.
steps.whatsHappening: The prayer leader explains that his merit comes from teaching תורה to children with fairness, generosity, and patience.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His merit has three parts. He treats poor and rich children equally. He teaches for free when a family cannot pay. He works lovingly to bring back students who are struggling. His dedication to teaching תורה to children is what made his prayer so powerful.

keyTerms.meaning: I bribe, I win him over

steps.whatToRemember: In both stories, rain came through the merit of the prayer leader's quiet good deeds, more than through the great sage's fast. One helped a poor town do its מצוות. The other taught תורה to every child with fairness and patience.
steps.whyThisMatters: These stories show that prayers can be answered through the merit of quietly serving the community, whether by providing for others' מצוות or by teaching children תורה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am a teacher of young children,
and I teach the children of the poor like the children of the rich.
And anyone who cannot afford it —
I do not take anything from him.
And I have a fishpond,
and anyone who neglects his studies,
I bribe him with them (the fish),
and we settle him and soothe him
until he comes and reads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's question from step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His merit is teaching all children equally, often for free, and patiently bringing back students who are struggling.

steps.title: רב נחמן's fast fails until he is humbled
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן declares a fast and prays, but no rain comes. In despair he says, 'Take נחמן and throw him from the wall to the ground.' He becomes broken-hearted, and the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן decreed a fast and prayed for mercy, but rain did not come. He said: 'Take נחמן and throw him off the wall to the ground!' He became deeply upset, and the rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new short story about a fast for rain. רב נחמן's prayer fails at first, and it is answered only after he feels crushed and humbled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two stories just before this one showed rain coming because of a prayer leader's good deeds. This story returns to the pattern of רבי יהודה נשיאה (steps 30-32): a leader's broken, humbled heart brings the rain. רב נחמן treats himself as worthless because his fast did not help, and that very feeling of lowliness is what brings the rain.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind became weak; he felt crushed, upset, humbled

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is talking about HIMSELF. He is not telling anyone to throw another person named נחמן off a wall. He speaks in the third person out of distress, as if to say: 'A leader whose fast does nothing deserves to be thrown down.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that humility and a broken heart can be a powerful key to having prayers answered, alongside good deeds.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman decreed a fast,
he prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
He said: Take Nachman
and throw him from the wall to the ground.
phrases.notes: He is voicing despair that his fast was useless.

phrases.english: He became upset, and rain came.
phrases.notes: His feeling of lowliness and humility is what brought the rain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story in the series of fasts for rain. It mirrors רבי יהודה נשיאה's story (steps 30-32): the fast fails, the leader is humbled (חלש דעתיה), and then rain comes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A leader's sincere feeling of humility and brokenness can bring an answer to prayer.

steps.title: רבה's fast also fails
steps.stepSummary: רבה declares a fast and prays, but no rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה decreed a fast and prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins another story about a fast that did not work. This line sets up the question that people will ask רבה next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording matches the opening of the רב נחמן story word for word. This time, though, the story does not end with rain. It leads into a challenge: why do some great leaders succeed when others do not?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked for mercy; he prayed

phrases.english: Rabba decreed a fast.
He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story with the same opening wording as the רב נחמן story. It sets up a comparison between generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה's fast did not bring rain. This sets the scene for the question that follows.

steps.title: People point out that רב יהודה's fasts brought rain
steps.stepSummary: People challenge רבה: when רב יהודה used to declare a fast, rain would come. Why not for you?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But look, when רב יהודה used to decree a fast, rain would come!
steps.whatsHappening: People question רבה and compare him to the earlier leader רב יהודה. Their question implies that something must be lacking in רבה's generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְהָא ('but look') signals a challenge, not just a request for information. The people are saying: we know fasts can work, because they worked for רב יהודה, so why is yours failing? This pushes רבה to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: An earlier great sage (a generation before רבה) whose fasts brought rain
When he used to (a repeated past action)

phrases.english: They said to him: But look, Rav Yehuda
when he would decree a fast,
rain would come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבה's failed fast by contrasting it with רב יהודה's successful ones.
steps.kashyaTarget: The worthiness of רבה and his generation, given that his fast failed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fasts worked in רב יהודה's day. If רבה's fast fails, it seems his generation is less worthy.

steps.title: רבה begins to answer: we study more תורה than they did
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers: what can I do? If the difference were about תורה study, we are actually greater than רב יהודה's generation, because in his years all their learning... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What can I do? If it is because of תורה study, we are greater than them, because in the years of רב יהודה all of their learning...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins to reply to the challenge. He argues that the difference cannot be about תורה learning, since his generation learns more. The amud ends mid-sentence, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה rejects the obvious explanation that his generation is weaker in תורה. He starts to prove that his generation's learning is broader than רב יהודה's. This sets up the point that something other than תורה study must explain why רב יהודה's fasts worked.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is NOT finished here. 'All of their learning...' continues on the next amud, where רבה explains what was limited about the learning in רב יהודה's day. Do not try to complete the thought yet.

phrases.english: He said to them: What can I do?
If it is because of Torah study,
we are superior to them,
as in the years of Rav Yehuda, all of their learning
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַאי אֶעֱבֵיד? אִי מִשּׁוּם תַּנּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by ruling out Torah study as the reason for the difference.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ruling out a suggested explanation (the answer is still in progress)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רבה's generation is weaker in תורה learning, and that is why rain does not come.
steps.terutzMaskana: תורה learning is not the reason, since רבה's generation learns more. The real reason is explained on the next amud.
